questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests basic CKAD concepts: PVC-backed watches, policy-driven validation, InitContainers, Secrets, sidecars, network policies, and external API reporting.

## Key Concepts

- Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap, Secret
- YAML validation with yq/jq; policy-driven checks
- InitContainer and TLS-sidecar patterns
- NetworkPolicy egress controls; readiness/liveness probes

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton: policy-watcher Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: policy-watcher
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: pods-pvc
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: pods-pvc
      - name: policies
        configMap:
          name: policy-config
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.19
        command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache yq jq"]
      containers:
      - name: watcher
        image: <registry>/policy-watcher:latest
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: api-creds
        volumeMounts:
        - name: pods-pvc
          mountPath: /pods
        - name: policies
          mountPath: /policies
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this in CI for policy regressions?
- What happens when policy-config changes at runtime?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests InitContainer sequencing, one-time data seeding, ConfigMap usage, and ensuring idempotent seeds and probes work with startup order.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers run before app containers
- Seed data via idempotent SQL (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
- Mount seed script from ConfigMap
- Probes and resource requests/limits to keep health
- Validation under load and restart scenarios

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: inventory
  namespace: retail
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-data
        image: postgres:15
        command: ["psql", "-h", "inventory-db", "-U", "seeduser", "-d", "inventory"]
        args: ["-f", "/seed/init.sql"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: seed-scripts
          mountPath: /seed
        env:
        - name: PGPASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: inventory-db-secret
              key: password
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: inventory-app:latest
        env:
        - name: DB_HOST
          value: "inventory-db"
        - name: DB_USER
          value: "seeduser"
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: inventory-db-secret
              key: password
      volumes:
      - name: seed-scripts
        configMap:
          name: inventory-seed-scripts
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you avoid reseeding when pods are rescheduled and during upgrades?
- How would you test seed idempotency and monitor seed success during rolling updates?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to coordinate InitContainers, sidecars, and config-driven apps in CKAD. Ensures proper volume mounting, file-based reloading semantics, and safe network posture.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer: pre-flight yamllint validation of /configs
- Config mounting: PVC-backed /configs shared with main container and sidecar
- Sidecar watcher: detects changes and triggers in-app reload via /reload/trigger
- Readiness/Liveness probes: ensure proper pod health
- Namespace NetworkPolicy: restricts egress to internal services only

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal skeleton (Deployment)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-reloader
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-reloader
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: lint-configs
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "yamllint /configs/**/*.yaml || exit 1"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /configs
      containers:
      - name: main-app
        image: myapp:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /configs
        - name: reload-volume
          mountPath: /reload
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        env:
        - name: RELOAD_PATH
          value: /reload/trigger
      - name: reload-watcher
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "inotifywait -m /configs -e modify,create -e moved_to | while read; do touch /reload/trigger; done"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /configs
        - name: reload-volume
          mountPath: /reload
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: config-pvc
      - name: reload-volume
        emptyDir: {}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you add multi-namespace isolation for this pattern?
- What happens on YAML syntax error after initial validation?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and runtime verification in CKAD scope, including namespace policies, container security, probes, and network controls.

## Key Concepts
- PodSecurity via namespace labels
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities
- Probes: readiness and liveness
- PreStop lifecycle
- ConfigMap mounting and rolling restarts via checksum
- NetworkPolicy egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch sketch (Deployment + NetworkPolicy)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: logger
  namespace: logging
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: logger
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: logger
        image: registry.example/logger:1.0
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cfg
          mountPath: /etc/logger
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /livez
            port: 8080
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
      volumes:
      - name: cfg
        configMap:
          name: logger-config
```

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: logger-egress
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: logger
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9200
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the rollback path if the ConfigMap causes a regression?
- How would you audit namespace security changes for compliance?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Validates CKAD basics: Jobs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, probes in a practical data-migrate flow.
- Introduces idempotence with a marker, a common real-world concern.

Key Concepts
- Job lifecycle and completion guarantees
- InitContainer usage for tooling installation
- Runtime config from ConfigMaps and Secrets
- PVC-based idempotence markers and backoff settings
- Probes and minimal YAML scaffolding

Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Job skeleton (pseudo)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-migrate
spec:
  backoffLimit: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: csvkit-install
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache python3 py3-pip && pip3 install csvkit"]
      containers:
      - name: migrator
        image: curlimages/curl:7.88.0
        command: ["sh", "-c", "python3 migrate.py"]
        env:
        - name: MIG_BATCH_SIZE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: mig-config
              key: MIG_BATCH_SIZE
        - name: API_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: mig-creds
              key: api-token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data/migrate
        - name: marker
          mountPath: /data/marker
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: migrate-pvc
      - name: marker
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: migrate-marker-pvc
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      # probes would be defined on the migrator container
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you test idempotence across retries?
- How would you handle partial CSV failures and ensure exactly-once semantics?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Practical CKAD tasks using ConfigMaps, env injection, probes, resources, and Service exposure. Demonstrates understanding of update strategies.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap usage via env/ENV
- Probes: readiness and liveness
- Resource requests/limits
- Service exposure and port mapping
- Rolling updates and rollout verification

## Code Example

```javascript
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: api-config
data:
  PORT: 3000
  APP_MODE: prod

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
template:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: api
  spec:
    containers:
    - name: api
      image: my-api:1.0
      ports:
      - containerPort: 3000
      env:
      - name: PORT
        valueFrom:
          configMapKeyRef:
            name: api-config
            key: PORT
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 3000
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 3000
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 100m
          memory: 128Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 200m
          memory: 256Mi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: api
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you reload config without pod restart?
- How do you verify a rolling update complete with zero downtime?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical token rotation using common CKAD primitives: InitContainer, Secrets, CronJob, and network policies in a per-namespace context.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for pre-population of credentials
- Secret storage and re-mounts on rotation
- CronJob for periodic credential refresh
- RBAC least privilege for Vault access
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton outline (not full manifests):
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: app-token
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: fetch-token
        image: curl:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "curl -sS https://vault.local/token -o /tokens/token.txt"]
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tokens
          name: token-vol
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tokens
          name: token-vol
      volumes:
      - name: token-vol
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: rotate-token
spec:
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: rotator
            image: curl:latest
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives for practical automation: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and PVCs, plus robust scheduling and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and jobTemplate usage
- ConfigMap and Secret as environment sources
- PVC mounting in Jobs for persistent backups
- Concurrency policy and job history controls
- Rollback and validation workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: dataops
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 7
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: postgres-backup
            image: postgres:15
            env:
            - name: BACKUP_DIR
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: BACKUP_DIR
            - name: DB_HOST
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: DB_HOST
            - name: DB_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_USER
            - name: DB_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_PASSWORD
            command:
            - /bin/bash
            - -c
            - |
              DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)
              BACKUP_FILE="/backups/${DB_NAME}-${DATE}.sql"
              pg_dump -h $DB_HOST -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME > $BACKUP_FILE
            volumeMounts:
            - name: backup-storage
              mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
          - name: backup-storage
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Validation Plan
1. Check CronJob creation: `kubectl get cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Verify schedule: `kubectl describe cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
3. Test manual job: `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/db-backup test-backup -n dataops`
4. Monitor job completion: `kubectl get jobs -n dataops -w`
5. Validate backup files: `kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n dataops -- ls -la /backups`

## Rollback Plan
1. Delete CronJob: `kubectl delete cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Clean up test jobs: `kubectl delete jobs -l job-name=db-backup -n dataops`
3. Remove backup files if needed: Access PVC and delete specific backup files
4. Recreate with corrected manifest if issues persist

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical hardening: container securityContext, readiness/liveness, graceful shutdown, high-availability with PDB, and network isolation via NetworkPolicy.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext and container securityContext
- Probes and lifecycle hooks
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy basics and egress constraints
- Per-namespace isolation in production-grade CKAD

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
  namespace: secure
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: api:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/api-config
        - name: secret
          mountPath: /etc/api-secret
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /readyz
            port: 8080
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
      volumes:
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-config
      - name: secret
        secret:
          secretName: api-secret
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-pdb
  namespace: secure
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-egress
  namespace: secure
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
      ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.0/12
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
      namespaceSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor and validate performance under load?
- How would you rollback the namespace isolation changes safely?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical CKAD skills: dynamic configuration via ConfigMaps, per-namespace isolation, InitContainers, health checks, logging, and network policy considerations.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped ConfigMaps**: Enable dynamic feature flags without pod restarts
- **InitContainers**: Provide bootstrap tooling (curl) before the main container starts
- **Conditional sidecars**: Driven by ConfigMap values to enable canary deployments
- **Readiness and liveness probes**: Ensure controller and application health
- **PVC-backed logs**: Provide persistent storage for debugging and audit trails
- **NetworkPolicies**: Enforce zero-trust networking by restricting egress to known endpoints

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Consideration |
|--------|----------------|
| **Polling Interval** | Frequent polls increase API load; infrequent polls delay flag propagation |
| **ConfigMap Updates** | Applications must watch or periodically read the ConfigMap to detect changes |
| **Sidecar Overhead** | Running a sidecar even when disabled consumes resources; consider whether the main container can react to flag changes directly |
| **Egress Restriction** | Locking down NetworkPolicy requires knowing all upstream dependencies upfront |
| **Log Persistence** | PVCs add operational complexity and cost; consider external logging solutions for production |

## Minimal YAML Skeleton

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
  namespace: feature-flags
data:
  flags.json: '{}'
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: logs-pvc
  namespace: feature-flags
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flag-poller
  namespace: feature-flags
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flag-poller
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flag-poller
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-curl
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'cp /usr/bin/curl /tools/curl']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
      containers:
        - name: poller
          image: your-poller-image:latest
          command: ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'while true; do curl -s $FLAGS_API > /config/flags.json; sleep 60; done']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: sidecar
          image: your-sidecar-image:latest
          env:
            - name: FEATURE_ENABLED
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-flags
                  key: enabled
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: feature-flags
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: logs-pvc
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: flags-egress-policy
  namespace: feature-flags
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flag-poller
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: flags-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
```

This design balances flexibility with operational simplicity, making it well-suited for Kubernetes feature management in multi-tenant environments.
